newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge rejects bid to stop Foccart's memoirs.
newsitem.headline: French judge rejects bid to stop Foccart's memoirs.

text.p: A Paris judge on Friday rejected a bid by the heir of Jacques Foccart to stop publication of the next instalment of the veteran French Africa policymaker's memoirs.
The judge ruled there was no evidence that Foccard, who died last week aged 83, had wanted the second volume of "Foccart speaks out" to be withdrawn.
Foccart's sole heir, 76-year-old Robert Rigaud, had taken publishing house Fayard to court to stop publication unless he was allowed to review the proofs before the book is released on April 9.
Some press reports said Foccart postponed publishing the book when he resumed his role as presidential adviser on African policy after President Jacques Chirac was elected in 1995.
Other reports have said Foccart, who was close to many African heads of state, deferred publication until after his death because the book contains explosive revelations.
The first volume, published in 1995, left many gaps in his cloak-and-dagger career spanning a quarter of a century.
The second volume consists of a series of interviews in which Foccart discusses his behind-the-scene orchestration of French policy in Africa over 25 years.
A member of the late President Charles de Gaulle's inner circle, Foccart had a reputation for using dubious and violent methods to maintain or overthrow African leaders according to Paris' interests.
